1use crate::third_party::hayro_interpret::function::{Clamper, TupleVec, Values, interpolate};
2use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::bit_reader::BitReader;
3use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::Array;
4use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::Stream;
5use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::dict::keys::{BITS_PER_SAMPLE, DECODE, ENCODE, SIZE};
6use smallvec::SmallVec;
7
8/// A type 0 function (sampled function).
9#[derive(Debug)]
10pub(crate) struct Type0 {
11    sizes: IntVec,
12    /// PdfCraft patch (31): the samples in stream order, `range.len()` to a grid point, the
13    /// first input varying fastest. They were a hash map keyed by each grid point, built again
14    /// every time a shading using the function was painted.
15    samples: Vec<u32>,
16    /// PdfCraft patch (31): how many grid points one step along each input moves.
17    strides: SmallVec<[usize; 4]>,
18    clamper: Clamper,
19    range: TupleVec,
20    bits_per_sample: u8,
21    encode: TupleVec,
22    decode: TupleVec,
23}
24
25impl Type0 {
26    /// Create a new type 0 function.
27    pub(crate) fn new(stream: &Stream<'_>) -> Option<Self> {
28        let dict = stream.dict();
29        let bits_per_sample = dict.get::<u8>(BITS_PER_SAMPLE)?;
30
31        if !matches!(bits_per_sample, 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 24 | 32) {
32            error!("invalid bits per sample: {bits_per_sample}");
33
34            return None;
35        }
36
37        let clamper = Clamper::new(dict)?;
38        let range = clamper.range.clone()?;
39
40        if range.is_empty() {
41            warn!("encountered Type0 function with invalid range length 0.");
42
43            return None;
44        }
45
46        let sizes = dict.get::<Array<'_>>(SIZE)?.iter::<u32>().collect::<IntVec>();
47
48        let encode = dict.get::<TupleVec>(ENCODE).unwrap_or(sizes.iter().map(|s| (0.0, s.saturating_sub(1) as f32)).collect());
49
50        // PdfCraft patch: see `MAX_SAMPLE_VALUES`.
51        let Some(num_expected_entries) = sizes
52            .iter()
53            .try_fold(1usize, |n, s| n.checked_mul(*s as usize))
54            .filter(|entries| *entries <= MAX_SAMPLE_ENTRIES)
55            .and_then(|entries| entries.checked_mul(range.len()))
56            .filter(|n| *n <= MAX_SAMPLE_VALUES)
57        else {
58            warn!("Type0 function has too many samples");
59
60            return None;
61        };
62
63        let decode = dict.get::<TupleVec>(DECODE).unwrap_or(range.clone());
64
65        let mut data = {
66            let decoded = stream.decoded().ok()?;
67            let mut buf = vec![];
68            let mut reader = BitReader::new(&decoded);
69
70            while buf.len() < num_expected_entries
71                && let Some(data) = reader.read(bits_per_sample)
72            {
73                buf.push(data);
74            }
75
76            buf
77        };
78
79        if data.len() != num_expected_entries {
80            warn!("Type0 function didn't have the expected number of sample entries.");
81            data.truncate(num_expected_entries);
82        }
83
84        // Saturating: the grid has at most `MAX_SAMPLE_ENTRIES` points unless a size is 0, and
85        // then no point is on it (`entry` checks each coordinate against its size first).
86        let mut strides = SmallVec::with_capacity(sizes.len());
87        let mut stride = 1usize;
88        for size in &sizes {
89            strides.push(stride);
90            stride = stride.saturating_mul(*size as usize);
91        }
92
93        Some(Self { sizes, clamper, range, bits_per_sample, samples: data, strides, encode, decode })
94    }
95
96    /// Evaluate a type 0 function with the given input.
97    pub(crate) fn eval(&self, mut input: Values) -> Option<Values> {
98        if input.len() != self.sizes.len() {
99            warn!("wrong number of arguments for sampled function");
100
101            return None;
102        }
103
104        self.clamper.clamp_input(&mut input);
105
106        let mut key = input;
107
108        for (((x, domain), encode), size) in key.iter_mut().zip(self.clamper.domain.iter()).zip(self.encode.iter()).zip(self.sizes.iter()) {
109            *x = interpolate(*x, domain.0, domain.1, encode.0, encode.1);
110            *x = x.max(0.0).min(*size as f32 - 1.0);
111        }
112
113        let in_prev = key.iter().map(|v| v.floor() as u32).collect::<IntVec>();
114        let in_next = key.iter().map(|v| v.ceil() as u32).collect::<IntVec>();
115        let mut coord: IntVec = in_prev.clone();
116
117        let interpolated = self.interpolate(&key, &in_prev, &in_next, &mut coord, 0)?;
118
119        // PdfCraft patch (31): `2_u32.pow(32)` overflowed (a panic with overflow checks on).
120        let max_sample = ((1u64 << self.bits_per_sample) - 1) as f32;
121        let mut out = interpolated
122            .iter()
123            .zip(self.decode.iter())
124            .map(|(x, decode)| interpolate(*x, 0.0, max_sample, decode.0, decode.1))
125            .collect::<SmallVec<_>>();
126
127        self.clamper.clamp_output(&mut out);
128
129        Some(out)
130    }
131}
132
133type FloatVec = SmallVec<[f32; 4]>;
134type IntVec = SmallVec<[u32; 4]>;
135
136// See <https://github.com/apache/pdfbox/blob/bb778d4784f354c36ce032e91a0cee2169a4c598/pdfbox/src/main/java/org/apache/pdfbox/pdmodel/common/function/PDFunctionType0.java#L252>
137impl Type0 {
138    /// PdfCraft patch (31): the value at `input` between the grid points `in_prev` and
139    /// `in_next`, interpolating the inputs from `step` on (the earlier ones are placed in
140    /// `coord`). The same multilinear interpolation, in the same order, as the hash-map
141    /// version, so the results are bit for bit the same; one level of recursion per input,
142    /// as before.
143    fn interpolate(&self, input: &[f32], in_prev: &[u32], in_next: &[u32], coord: &mut IntVec, step: usize) -> Option<FloatVec> {
144        let (Some(x), Some(prev), Some(next)) = (input.get(step), in_prev.get(step), in_next.get(step)) else {
145            // Every input placed: the grid point itself.
146            return Some(self.entry(coord)?.iter().map(|n| *n as f32).collect());
147        };
148        let (x, prev, next) = (*x, *prev, *next);
149
150        *coord.get_mut(step)? = prev;
151        let val1 = self.interpolate(input, in_prev, in_next, coord, step + 1)?;
152        if prev == next {
153            return Some(val1);
154        }
155        *coord.get_mut(step)? = next;
156        let val2 = self.interpolate(input, in_prev, in_next, coord, step + 1)?;
157
158        Some(val1.iter().zip(val2.iter()).map(|(a, b)| interpolate(x, prev as f32, next as f32, *a, *b)).collect())
159    }
160
161    /// PdfCraft patch (31): the samples of grid point `coord`, or `None` where it is off the
162    /// grid or the stream ended before it (where the hash map had no entry).
163    fn entry(&self, coord: &[u32]) -> Option<&[u32]> {
164        let mut index = 0usize;
165        for ((c, size), stride) in coord.iter().zip(&self.sizes).zip(&self.strides) {
166            if c >= size {
167                return None;
168            }
169            index = index.checked_add((*c as usize).checked_mul(*stride)?)?;
170        }
171        let n = self.range.len();
172        let start = index.checked_mul(n)?;
173        self.samples.get(start..start.checked_add(n)?)
174    }
175}
176
177/// PdfCraft patch: the most sample values a sampled function may have, and the most table
178/// entries (one per point of its `/Size` grid). The samples were read into 4-byte values and
179/// then into a table entry each, so a stream inflating to 256 MiB of 1-bit samples asked for
180/// 8 GB; `/Size` sets how many the table expects. The largest real tables are DeviceN tint
181/// transforms: 33 × 33 × 33 × 33 points with 3 outputs is 1.2 million entries and 3.6 million
182/// values, 17^5 points with 4 outputs 5.7 million values.
183const MAX_SAMPLE_VALUES: usize = 1 << 23;
184const MAX_SAMPLE_ENTRIES: usize = 1 << 21;
